Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Cassius Dio Cocceianus (author, Wikidata Q185223), died 250; Herbert Baldwin Foster (translator, Wikidata Q1608010), died 1906. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Cassius Dio Cocceianus, 165?-235?; Foster, Herbert Baldwin, 1874-1906 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's (Wikidata gives some of them several death years, every one 1925 or earlier: Cassius Dio Cocceianus [229, 235, 250]).

Printed edition: Dio's Rome: An Historical Narrative Originally Composed in Greek During the Reigns of Septimus ..., Pafraets Book Co., 1905, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/diosromeanhisto05zonagoog. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 69%, 76%, 93% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Cassius Dio Cocceianus, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
